pushback_verification: All 7 verified against current artifact content before disposition; none suppressed as stale. The CRITICAL was confirmed by reading both halves of the contradiction in place — the fallback's absence trigger and the scope rule's unattached-equals-pre-capability clause — and by confirming `new`/`continue` produce no attachment. The branch-reuse warning was confirmed against the choreography's stated ordering and the compatibility definition; the reviewer had already reproduced the git refusal in a disposable repository.

resolutions.title: An absent attachment both triggers discovery and prohibits the tail
resolutions.action: A WHOLLY ABSENT `pr_attachment` now TERMINATES the PR path before any remote or `gh` work; the fallback query serves ONE narrow case — an attachment that EXISTS but lacks `url` (branch work succeeded, PR creation failed). This closes a contradiction created by this cycle's own attachment-authority ratification: absence meant unattached-and-pre-capability in the scope rule while simultaneously triggering discovery in the rule above it. The concrete failure is named in the requirement — `/orbit:new` + `/orbit:continue` never produce an attachment, so a change started that way whose branch name matched a hand-opened PR would have been committed, pushed, rewritten, and flipped after a consent preview that omitted the outward-writes line precisely because the change is unattached. Scenario + task 4.2.

resolutions.title: `pr: never` has incompatible output contracts
resolutions.action: Defined resolution order as CONFIG FIRST, AVAILABILITY SECOND. Absent/`never`/inert config returns IMMEDIATELY — probing nothing (no remote enumeration, no `gh`) and emitting no availability note, so `never`'s promise of byte-identical silence holds in a repo that also lacks a remote. Availability resolution and its degradation note run ONLY once a recognized ACTIVE mode is selected. Also stated that inert-value and invalid-shape warnings are independent of availability: they name a config problem, need no probe, and are never suppressed or duplicated by a degradation note that will not run.

resolutions.title: Compatible per-proposal branches can be impossible to reuse at the specified seam
resolutions.action: Ratified option A — the choreography is now THREE ORDERED PHASES with branch selection FIRST: (1) resolve, validate, and SWITCH to the target branch, local-only, before any artifact exists; (2) generate and validate on that branch; (3) outward writes only after validation succeeds. The old ordering mandated an impossible step — a compatible per-proposal branch is DEFINED as carrying this change's artifact commits, so it already tracks the paths generation had just written as untracked files, and `git switch` refuses rather than overwrite them (the reviewer reproduced this in a disposable repo). Reachable by an ordinary sequence: propose, degrade for want of `gh`, fix, propose again. The guarantee that nothing leaves the machine before validation is preserved exactly, since phase 1 is local-only; a validation failure now leaves the user on the target branch and the note NAMES it with `git switch <default>` as recovery. Preconditions restated as phase-1 (a skip writes nothing and the change proceeds unattached); two scenarios and two harness cases added.

resolutions.title: Archive failures strand a non-rerunnable tail without completion commands
resolutions.action: Brought EVERY tail step inside the degradation contract (staging and commit included, not only push/`gh`) and enumerated the four partial states with their repository-qualified completing command and consequence: staging/commit failed (`git add`+`commit`; writes present but uncommitted, PR untouched), push failed (`git push <resolved-remote> <branch>`; the PR lacks its own archive commit, which is why the ordering invariant already forbids the flip there), description rewrite failed (`gh pr edit <url> --body-file <path>`; PR current in code, stale intent narrative), flip failed (`gh pr ready --repo <owner>/<repo> <number>`; complete and accurate but DRAFT — a safe resting state). Stated explicitly that `/orbit:archive` is NOT a retry path, since the change has already moved and emitted.

resolutions.title: Arc-done lookup validates a recorded URL but defines no invalid-URL branch
resolutions.action: Ratified option A. Defined THREE validation outcomes under one invariant — the readout is NEVER SUPPRESSED, because arc-done is surfaced once per program and a silent readout is indistinguishable from an unfinished program: valid → surface; query FAILED → surface with `state unverified`; positively INVALID (closed, merged, retargeted, foreign repository) → FALL THROUGH to the constrained `--head <program-branch>` query and surface what it finds, or state that no open replacement exists. Recorded why this is deliberately the OPPOSITE of the archive tail's answered-not-retried rule: the seams differ in RISK, not vocabulary — the tail writes, so a second chance there could rewrite and flip the wrong PR, while this readout only reports and the worst a fall-through can do is name a better URL.
resolutions.resolution: A — fall through to the constrained query on positive invalidity; never suppress the readout

resolutions.title: Attachment state is not permanently draft by construction
resolutions.action: Corrected the premise while keeping the conclusion: `pr_attachment.state` is a POINT-IN-TIME OBSERVATION recorded at the attaching invocation and never updated, so it goes stale whatever its initial value — usually `"draft"`, but legitimately `"ready"` for an ADOPTED program PR, which is why the schema admits both. The consequence is now stated symmetrically: a readout gated on the recorded value would either nag forever after the human flips READY, or fall silent against a PR since reopened as a draft.

resolutions.title: The no-CI probe has no specified Git ref
resolutions.action: Bound the check to ONE ref — the resolved remote's default-branch ref, the same ref branch creation uses and one the existence check has already fetched — never the pre-switch worktree and never the target branch. Those three can disagree (a long-lived program branch may carry workflows the base lacks, or the reverse), and the note describes the CI context the NEW PR INHERITS, which is the base's.

final_assessment: 7 of 7 resolved; 0 unresolved markers in scope. The reviewer's diagnosis — authority at NEGATIVE and PARTIAL states — held: the happy paths carried strong identity constraints while 'no attachment', 'invalid recorded URL', and 'some tail steps already completed' each still admitted materially different outward decisions. Two decision-lane findings ratified in chat. The CRITICAL was self-inflicted by this cycle's own attachment-authority ratification and would have allowed an unpreviewed push on an explicitly out-of-scope path. The branch-reuse finding identified a specified path that could not execute at all, resolved by reordering propose into three phases with local-only selection first — the largest structural change of this cycle, and one that strengthens rather than weakens the nothing-leaves-the-machine-before-validation guarantee. Capabilities 7; tasks 31; fingerprints 4/4 verified; strict validation passes; 1918 tests green.
